mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of quarters where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses wage growth and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of two consecutive months with UNRATE > 6.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly rise of at least 0.5% in both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad-based acceleration in economic activity, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO and HOUST both rise > 0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in at least 70% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month spike in the federal funds rate above 5% without a concurrent rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals a policy-driven rate shock that increases risk premiums and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 5% and CPIAUCSL change < 0.1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 5-day returns in more than 50% of policy-shock months defined by the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 1% for three consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-facing firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during three-month periods of sustained RSAFS declines > 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 95 for two consecutive months signals a broad-based supply-side recession, which reduces corporate earnings and increases downside risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods where INDPRO remains below 95 for two consecutive months.
